headline: US stocks closed lower as AI slowdown fears weighed on tech and chipmakers while surging oil and a near-5% 10-year yield sharpened focus on this week’s FOMC meeting
raw_text:
- The S&P 500 ($SPX) fell 0.48% to 7,619.98, the Dow ($DJI) slipped 0.29% to 52,421.20, and the Nasdaq ($COMP) lost 0.56%, marking the S&P’s fifth decline in six sessions and leaving it 2.3% below its August 13 record close of 7,798.99.
- AI slowdown fears tied to AI safety calls from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic co-founder Dario Amodei pressured chipmakers and broader technology shares.
- The 10-year Treasury yield briefly hit 5.012% intraday before easing to around 4.96% as rising oil prices added to inflation worries.
- Communication Services led with a 2.8% gain, driven by Netflix (NFLX) after Evercore ISI upgraded the stock and raised its price target to $110 on live programming potential, while Health Care and Consumer Staples rose modestly and Information Technology lagged with a 1.6–1.7% decline.
- Cybersecurity stocks rallied on the AI safety theme, with Zscaler (ZS) up 16.5%, Rubrik (RBRK) up 15.6%, SentinelOne (S) up 14.5%, Palo Alto Networks (PANW) up 13.3%, and CrowdStrike (CRWD) jumping 13.85% to $235.38.
- Chip and AI infrastructure names weakened, with Corning (GLW) down 13.7%, Coherent (COHR) off 12.7%, and other chip-related stocks such as Teradyne (TER) and Nvidia (NVDA) lower, with Nvidia (NVDA) off roughly 3–3.4% on AI demand concerns.
- Bank of America (BAC) slid about 5.1% to $59.47 after forecasting a more than 10% drop in third-quarter investment banking fees, raising concerns about softer deal-making revenue.
- Oil prices climbed sharply, with Brent crude (@QA) above $105 and WTI (@CL) over $101 per barrel after Saudi Arabia shut a key pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz due to attacks, boosting inflation concerns and reinforcing expectations for tighter policy.
- Few after-hours earnings, including small caps such as Dave & Buster’s (PLAY) and Radiant Logistics (RLGT), produced moves of more than 2%, as attention shifted to this week’s two-day FOMC meeting, where futures are pricing roughly a 90% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike to 4.0% on Wednesday.
